summary: Christian Lindtner (1953–2020) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his filosofiske doktorgrad at the University of Copenhagen by 1982 and served as a professor there (attested 1980–1991).

Christian Luczanits is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He earned his Magister (1994) and Ph.D. (1998) at the University of Vienna, and held posts at Vienna, Stanford, UC Berkeley, and the Rubin Museum of Art.

Christian Wittern is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies who studied under Seizan Yanagida. He held posts as professor at Kyoto University (attested 1993, 2008) and Hanazono University (attested 2011).

Christianus Cornelis Uhlenbeck (1866–1951) was a linguist and Indologist. After studying at Stedelijk Gymnasium Haarlem and Leiden University (~1884–1888), he held positions at the University of Amsterdam (1892–1899) and Leiden University (1899–1926).

Christine Chojnacki is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. She completed her doctoral thesis at Sorbonne Nouvelle University in 1991 and served as a professor at Jean Moulin University Lyon 3 (attested 2018).

Christine Mollier is a scholar of Sinology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who studied under Kristofer Schipper. She was a researcher (1989–1995) and Director of Research (attested 2014) at CNRS, and a visiting professor at the University of Chicago.

Christof Zotter works in Indology and religious studies. In 2018, he was attested as head of the editorial program and postdoctoral researcher at the Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities, and as an editorial board member for Documenta Nepalica.

Christoph Anderl (born 1963) is a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He earned his MA at the University of Vienna (~1989–1995) and completed his PhD at the University of Oslo (~1999–2004) under Christoph Harbsmeier.

Christoph Cüppers (born 1948) is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Hamburg (~1977–1983) under Lambert Schmithausen, Srinivasa Ayya Srinivasan, and Albrecht Wezler, and directed the Lumbini International Research Institute (~1993–2013).

Christoph Emmrich (born 1965) specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Heidelberg (PhD 2004), where he held an attested post in 2001, and served as Assistant Professor at the University of Toronto.

Christoph Harbsmeier (born 1946) is a Sinologist and linguist. Educated at Merton College, Oxford, and Copenhagen (Ph.D. ~1973–1981), he held posts at Universiti Sains Malaysia, University of Oslo (Professor from 1980), Peking University, Fudan, and Shanghai Normal University.

Christoph Kleine (born 1962) specializes in religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Marburg and Bukkyo University, he held posts at EFEO, Hōbōgirin, Marburg, Leipzig (Privatdozent 2002–2005; Professor 2008), and Munich (Professor 2004–2008).

Christoph Theodosius Walther (1699–1741) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied theology at the University of Halle (1720) and served as a missionary with the Danish-Halle Mission (~1725–1739).

Christoph von Fürer-Haimendorf (1909–1995) studied at Vienna (Dr. phil 1931, Habilitation 1939) and the LSE. He was a professor at Vienna, Osmania University, University College London, and SOAS University of London (1950–1976).
Christophe Jaffrelot (born 1964) is an Indologist who studied at Sciences Po (~1985–1991) under Jean Leca. He held posts at CNRS (from ~1991) and Sciences Po (from ~1999).
Christophe Vielle is an Indologist. He has held teaching posts at KU Leuven as professor of Sanskrit (attested 2009) and at Université catholique de Louvain as professor (attested 2013).

Christopher Byrne specializes in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at McGill University (attested 2015), where he was supervised by Grace S. Fong and G. Victor Sōgen Hori, and taught by Robin D. S. Yates.
Christopher D. Emms is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at McMaster University under doctoral supervisor Shayne Clarke (attested 2012).

Christopher G. Framarin is a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He earned an M.A. from the University of Hawaiʻi (2001), a Ph.D. from the University of New Mexico (2005), and became associate professor at the University of Calgary (attested 2014).
Christopher Hatchell is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who earned his Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Virginia under the academic mentorship of David F. Germano.
